answer: `Ctrl-Alt-c` (or `Cmd-Alt-c` on Mac) runs `Comment: Add`, which inserts a comment after the current block. You can also use the `/comment` slash command.

Memory for: What's the keyboard shortcut for inserting a comment block after the current block?
[1] Markdown/Comment.md (Use cases)
  Commands: * `Comment: Add` (`Ctrl-Alt-c` / `Cmd-Alt-c`, or the `/comment` slash command) inserts a comment after the current block. / * `Comment: Selection` wraps the selected lines in `<!--` and `-->`.
[2] Guide/Comments, Mentions and Replies.md (Add a comment)
  Add a comment: SilverBullet leverage’s HTML-style [[Markdown/Comment]] syntax to add comments: / ```markdown / <!-- / Hello world! / --> / ``` / Which _Live Previews_ as follows: / <!-- / Hello world! / --> / For convenience, a few (slash) commands are available to make adding comments easier. / Put the cursor in the paragraph you want to discuss and run **Comment: Add** from the command palette, or use `/comment` on a new line. SilverBullet inserts a comment after the current block. If you select text first, **Comment: Add** quotes it inside the new comment.
  Find and answer it: 1. Run `Navigate: Mentions`, or click a mention to open the _Mention Inbox_. / 2. Select the recipient from the dropdown. The inbox normally starts with your own identity and groups entries by page. / 3. Open the request and write the answer underneath. Mention the original writer if the reply should appear in their inbox: / ```markdown / @author This section is ready for review. -- @reviewer / ``` / Use `Mention: Sign` or `/sign` to sign the current block as yourself. Signing alone credits the reply.
[3] Authorship.md (The `-- @name` notation)
  Signing your own text: Rather than typing the notation by hand, run `Mention: Sign` (or the `/sign` slash command) to append `-- @you` to the end of the current block. This is what lets a person answer a mention without re-queuing the reply in their own inbox: signing a reply attributes it, it does not address it, so it never becomes a fresh request to yourself.
[4] CHANGELOG.md (CHANGELOG)
  2.7.0: * Fix: symlinks inside the space directory are no longer accidentally removed when cleaning up empty parent directories after a file delete. / * Fix: slash commands now resolve the syntax node ending at the cursor, so they no longer get incorrectly suppressed adjacent to comment blocks or links. / * Fix: [Service Worker is now built without `import` statements](https://github.com/silverbulletmd/silverbullet/pull/1949) so it loads on Firefox versions before 147 (by [Carlos Fdez. Llamas](https://github.com/sirikon)).
[5] Slash Command.md (Built-in slash commands)
  Built-in slash commands: [[^Library/Std#Slash templates]] provides many useful ones out of the box. / **Editing** / * `/h1`, `/h2`, `/h3`, `/h4` — convert the current line into a heading of the given level / * `/task` — convert the current line into a task (`* [ ] ...`) / * `/frontmatter` — insert a YAML frontmatter block at the top of the page / * `/space-lua` — insert a `space-lua` fenced code block / **Dates** / * `/today` — insert today’s date (e.g. `2026-03-04`) / * `/yesterday` — insert yesterday’s date / * `/tomorrow` — inse ...
Exact facts:
- [1] A `space-lua` or `space-style` block inside a comment is _not_ indexed, and the pages read at boot ([[CONFIG]], [[Library|libraries]]) skip it as well, so commenting a script out is how you disable it.
- [1] What a comment does not switch off is live evaluation in the open editor: `${...}` [[Space Lua#Expressions|expressions]] and Lua-registered [[API/codeWidget|code widgets]] inside a comment still run and render, and a commented-out `space-lua` block is still linted for syntax errors.
